summary: Jeannine Auboyer worked in indology and history and archaeology. She studied at the École du Louvre, Académie Julian, and École Pratique des Hautes Études. She held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1980) and Musée Guimet (1965–1980).
Jeff Dolven studied at Worcester College (~1989–1991) and Yale University (~1992–1998). He founded Princeton University, where he held a post around 2001.
Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who served as Professor at the University of Tasmania (~1999) and held a post at La Trobe University in 2019.

Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at UNC Chapel Hill (~2004–2009) under Thomas A. Tweed and Richard M. Jaffe, also studying under mentors Taitetsu Unno and Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long works in indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1993–2000) and was appointed Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Clark Ruff studied at Missouri State and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White. In religious studies and indology, his posts include UNC Chapel Hill, Missouri State, UC Santa Barbara, Director at University of California, and Assistant Professor at Marshall (2002).

Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Washington (~1983–1991) under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox and advisor Sanghasen Singh.

Jeffrey Hopkins worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. From 1970 to 2005, he was an associate professor and director at the University of Virginia.

Jeffrey J. Kripal works in religious studies and indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1987–1993). In ~2002, he became Lynette S. Autrey Associate Professor in the Humanities at Rice University.
Jeffrey K. Riegel is a sinologist who served as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley (~1982–2007) and held a post at the University of Sydney (~2007–2017).

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Komazawa and Leiden under James A. Benn and Terry Russell. He held posts at McMaster University (~2018–2019) and the University of Bologna (~2021).

Jeffrey L. Broughton works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1968–1975) and became a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University, Long Beach (~1978).

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (~1974–1983) and Boston University (~1983), alongside positions at UC Berkeley, Harvard, Cornell, and Washington University in St. Louis.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson works in indology and philosophy. After studying at Harvard (~1961–1970), he held posts at the University of Toronto (~1970–1980), University of Michigan (~1981–1982), and UC Berkeley as Professor of Sanskrit (~1980–1992).
Jeffrey S. Lidke works in religious studies and indology. He served as visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia (~2000–2003) and held a post at Berry College (~2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia (~1996–2002) under Karen C. Lang and W. S. Karunatillake. He became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (~2003).
Jeffrey Stout is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Brown, Princeton, and the California Culinary Academy. He served as a professor at Princeton University from ~1975 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at UNC Wilmington, Tennessee, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen. He taught at UCLA (~2006–2013) and became a lecturer at UC San Diego (~2014).

Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1998–2006), studying under doctoral supervisors Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, as well as MA supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and indology. He served as Professor at the University of Oslo (1997) and at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (~2013).
